A1.text: Write a Ruby method `word_frequency(text)` that returns a hash of word => count, case-insensitive, ignoring punctuation, sorted by count descending. Use Enumerable methods idiomatically. Provide just the method definition.

A2.text: Write a Ruby class `Stack` with a properly encapsulated internal array (not exposed via attr_reader). Implement push, pop, peek, and empty? methods. Raise a custom error class `StackUnderflowError` when calling pop or peek on an empty stack.

A3.text: Write a Ruby method `safe_divide(a, b)` that divides a by b, gracefully handling ZeroDivisionError and TypeError. On error, print a warning message and return nil. On success, return the quotient.

A4.text: Write a Ruby method `extract_emails(text)` that uses a regular expression to extract all valid-looking email addresses from a block of text, returning them as a unique, sorted array.

B1.text: Write a Rails 7.1 migration that adds a `status` column (string, default "draft", not null) to an existing `articles` table, and adds a database index on that column.

B2.text: Write ActiveRecord validations for a Rails 7.1 `User` model: `email` must be present and unique (case-insensitive), `username` must be present with length between 3 and 20, and `age` must be numeric but may be nil.

B3.text: Write a Rails 7.1 controller action `PostsController#publish` (a member route) that transitions a post's status to "published" and sets `published_at` to the current time, then redirects back to the post with a flash notice on success, or a flash alert if the save fails.

B4.text: Add an enum to a Rails 7.1 `Order` model for `status` with values pending, paid, shipped, cancelled, using the `validate: true` option introduced in Rails 7.1. Also add a scope `recent` that returns orders created in the last 7 days, ordered by created_at descending.

B5.text: Write `config/routes.rb` entries for a resourceful `articles` route nested under an `admin` namespace, including a custom member route `publish` (POST) and a custom collection route `archived` (GET).

C1.text: Set up a background job in this Rails app to send a welcome email asynchronously when a user signs up.

C2.text: Add user authentication to this Rails app.

C3.text: Configure the asset pipeline for this Rails app to compile and serve a new stylesheet.

D1.text: Write a Rails model method `process_order` on an `Order` model that saves the order within a database transaction and enqueues an `OrderProcessorJob` to run afterward, ensuring the job cannot start running before the order is actually committed to the database.

D2.text: Write a Rails config snippet or initializer you would add to a Rails app to enable YJIT for better performance in production.

D3.text: Write a Rails initializer that checks the running Ruby version at application boot and raises a clear error if it is below the minimum Ruby version required by this Rails app.

D4.text: Write ActiveRecord model callbacks on an `Order` model: one that logs a message immediately after a database transaction successfully commits, and a separate one that logs a message when a transaction rolls back.

E1.text: Add pagination to the `ArticlesController#index` action using the Kaminari gem, showing 10 articles per page.

E2.text: Add file upload support to the `Article` model using Rails ActiveStorage, allowing a single attached image called `cover_image`.

E3.text: Add a fuzzy/partial-match search scope to the `Article` model using the ransack gem, searching across the `title` and `body` fields.

F1.text: Add a has_many :through association: a `Doctor` has_many :patients, through: :appointments, and an `Appointment` belongs_to both a `Doctor` and a `Patient`. Write the three model class bodies.

F2.text: Add a polymorphic `Comment` model (with a `body` text field) that can belong to either an `Article` or a `Post`, using Rails' polymorphic association pattern. Write the `Comment` model and the association lines needed on `Article` and `Post`.

F3.text: Add a callback to the `Order` model that sets `shipped_at` to the current time, but only when the `status` is changed to "shipped", and only after the record has actually been saved to the database.

F4.text: Extract shared 'archivable' behavior into a reusable Rails Concern: an `archived` boolean flag, an `archive!` method that sets it true and saves, and a `scope :active` that excludes archived records. Show the Concern module and how to include it in the `Article` and `Order` models.

F5.text: Write the strong parameters method in `ArticlesController` for a form that creates an `Article` and its associated `Comments` in one submission using nested attributes, permitting only the appropriate fields and not over-permitting.

G1.text: Write a Minitest integration or controller test for a Rails `PostsController#publish` action. The action transitions a post's status to "published", sets `published_at` to the current time, and redirects back to the post with a flash notice on success.

G2.text: Write a Minitest model test for a Rails `User` model with these validations: `email` must be present and unique (case-insensitive), `username` must be present with length between 3 and 20, and `age` must be numeric but may be nil.

R1.text: Write a Ruby method that builds a hash from local variables `name`, `age`, and `email`.

R2.text: Define an immutable Point value object with `x` and `y` attributes in Ruby.

R3.text: Write a Ruby method `wrapper` that accepts any arguments and forwards all of them, unnamed, to another method called `target`.

R4.text: Write a Ruby block that doubles each number in an array using the implicit block parameter shorthand, without naming the parameter explicitly.
